hook: Mineart began as a mechanical engineer at Caterpillar in 1999 and spent nearly three decades rising through engineering, product strategy, and electric power leadership roles before being named Chief Technology Officer, now leading Cat Technology's push to integrate smarter, more connected machines across Caterpillar's global equipment lines.
name: Jaime Mineart

quote.text: We don't just build smarter machines, we create integrated, scalable solutions that deliver real-world results.
quote.context: Jaime Mineart, personal LinkedIn profile summary

reading.body:
Jaime Mineart, now Caterpillar's Chief Technology Officer, spent the bulk of his career inside the electric power division, making him one of the few company-wide CTOs at a major equipment manufacturer whose expertise is grounded specifically in power generation and energy transition rather than software or electronics.

The trajectory from mechanical engineer in 1999 to CTO in 2025 ran directly through large diesel and electric power systems, product strategy, and commercial leadership for energy transition solutions. That path matters for AI infrastructure because Caterpillar is a primary supplier of generator sets and backup power systems for data centers. The person now setting Cat Technology's direction has spent years working on the exact products that keep compute facilities running when grid power is insufficient or unavailable.

The data does not cover Mineart's specific technology priorities as CTO, any announcements made since his appointment in 2025, or Caterpillar's internal strategy for AI-adjacent markets. What the record does establish is the institutional depth he brings: nearly three decades inside one company, with his most senior roles concentrated in electric power at precisely the moment data center power demand began straining grid capacity.
